description: Copy-paste Tailwind CSS page sections: heroes, features, how it works, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, calls to action, footers and content grids. Live previews at desktop, tablet and phone widths.
intro: Heroes, feature grids, testimonials, pricing, FAQs, footers. Each one renders live next to its code, at desktop, tablet or phone width, in light or dark mode.
beforeYouPaste:
• Tailwind CSS v4. Every snippet uses Tailwind v4 syntax, including the trailing ! (important) on some classes. Your site needs Tailwind v4 set up, which every BootForm template already has.
  • Your brand colour. Snippets use brand-50, brand-500 and brand-600. Define those three in your @theme block, or find and replace brand with a Tailwind colour such as indigo.
  • Why some classes end in !. Pasted into a VitePress page, VitePress's own styles for headings, paragraphs, links, lists and tables beat plain Tailwind classes. The ! goes exactly on the classes that would otherwise lose. Outside VitePress it does no harm.
  • Links and images. Links point at # and images come from Picsum Photos. Swap both for your own. On a VitePress site served from a subpath (GitHub Pages), write an internal link as :href="withBase('/contact')", not href="/contact".
  • Forms. The two sections with a form post to https://f.bootform.com/__YOUR_FORM_ID__. Generate your own form ID at bootform.com/uuidgenerator and claim it before the page goes live, or point action at any other backend.
  • Using Claude Code? The add-section skill in BootForm/site-skills pastes any of these into your page and adapts it for you.

categories.title: Heroes
categories.description: The first thing on the page. Every hero here stacks its buttons full-width on a phone and puts them side by side from 640px up.

sections.title: Centered
sections.description: Headline, one line of supporting text, two buttons. The safe default when you don't have a strong image.

sections.title: Split with image
sections.description: Text on the left, a photo on the right, stacked with the text first on a phone.

sections.title: Photo backdrop
sections.description: A full-width photo behind the text, with a dark overlay so white text stays readable on any picture. Grows with its content instead of clipping it.
notes: The overlay (bg-black/55) is what makes the text readable. On a very bright photo, raise it to bg-black/65.

sections.title: With a form
sections.description: The pitch on the left and a short quote-request form on the right. For a local business whose whole goal is one enquiry.
notes: Replace __YOUR_FORM_ID__ with your own form ID. Keep the hidden honeypot input: spam filtering depends on it being submitted empty.

sections.title: Announcement and screenshot
sections.description: A small badge linking to news, a centered headline, and a product screenshot in a browser frame underneath.

categories.title: Features
categories.description: What you do or what the product does. Five layouts, from a plain icon grid to tabs that work with no JavaScript.

sections.title: Icon grid
sections.description: Six short features in a grid: one column on a phone, two on a tablet, three on a desktop.

sections.title: Alternating image and text
sections.description: Two or three bigger features, each with its own image, alternating sides on a desktop and always image-first on a phone.

sections.title: Tabs
sections.description: One feature at a time, switched by tabs. Pure CSS: hidden radio buttons and Tailwind's has-[] variants, so it works in plain HTML and inside VitePress markdown alike.
notes: The radio ids (feature-tab-1 and so on) must be unique on the page. If you paste this twice, rename them in the second copy, including in the group-has-[#...] classes.

sections.title: Sticky heading
sections.description: The heading stays in view on the left while a list of features scrolls past on the right. On a phone it's a plain stacked list.
notes: md:top-24 leaves room for a 64px site header, which is VitePress's. Adjust it if your header is taller.

sections.title: Bento grid
sections.description: One large card and four small ones, in an uneven grid that collapses to a single column on a phone.

categories.title: How it works
categories.description: Three or four steps between a visitor and what they came for.

sections.title: Numbered steps
sections.description: Three steps side by side, each with a big number. One column on a phone.

sections.title: Timeline
sections.description: Steps down a vertical line. Works at any width, and holds more text per step than the numbered version.

categories.title: Social proof
categories.description: Why a visitor should believe you: what other people said, who uses you, and the numbers.

sections.title: Testimonial cards
sections.description: Three short quotes, each with a name, a role and an initials avatar, so nobody needs a headshot.
notes: Use real quotes from real customers, with their permission. Made-up testimonials are worse than none.

sections.title: Quote banner
sections.description: One big quote on its own. For the single testimonial that says it best.

sections.title: Logo strip
sections.description: A row of customer or partner names, greyed out so they don't compete with your own brand. The example names are made up.
notes: Swap each text wordmark for the real logo (an <img> or inline SVG), and only list companies that agreed to it.

sections.title: Stats row
sections.description: Three or four numbers with labels. Two columns on a phone, all in a row on a desktop.

categories.title: Pricing and FAQ
categories.description: What it costs, and the questions people ask before they decide.

sections.title: Two tiers
sections.description: Two plans side by side. The simplest pricing that still gives people a choice.

sections.title: Three tiers
sections.description: Three plans, with the middle one highlighted as the one most people pick. Stacked on a phone, in a row from 1024px.

sections.title: Comparison table
sections.description: Features down the side, plans across the top. Scrolls sideways on a phone instead of squashing the columns.
notes: The ! classes on the table, rows and cells are what stop VitePress's own table styles (striped rows, borders on every cell, display: block) from taking over.

sections.title: FAQ accordion
sections.description: Questions that open one at a time, built on <details>, so it works with no JavaScript and every answer is in the page for search engines.
notes: The shared name="faq" is what closes one answer when another opens. Remove it to let several stay open at once.

categories.title: Calls to action and footers
categories.description: The end of the page: one last push, a newsletter signup, and the footer.

sections.title: Call-to-action band
sections.description: A coloured panel with a headline and two buttons. Goes right before the footer.

sections.title: Newsletter band
sections.description: An email field and a button, side by side on a desktop and stacked on a phone.
notes: Replace __YOUR_FORM_ID__ with your own form ID. Keep the hidden honeypot input.

sections.title: Simple footer
sections.description: Your name, a few links and a copyright line. Enough for most small sites.

sections.title: Footer with columns
sections.description: A short blurb plus three columns of links. Two columns on a phone.
notes: On a VitePress site built from a BootForm template, the footer comes from docs/.vitepress/theme/index.ts, not from a page. Put the footer there, or leave the template's own one alone.

categories.title: Content
categories.description: Grids of things: articles or projects, people, photos.

sections.title: Card grid
sections.description: Image, title, a line of text and a link, three across on a desktop. For posts, projects or services.

sections.title: Team
sections.description: Names and roles with initials avatars. Swap an avatar for a photo when you have one.

sections.title: Photo gallery
sections.description: A grid of photos with one large feature image. Two columns on a phone, four on a desktop.
